answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when a bonded challenge proves the identity is duplicating claims or colluding. Rewards are capped per verified contribution, so spawning a thousand names does not multiply payout; the attacker must fund a thousand locks and risks losing them. A harbor may use timber deliveries as the example, with delta checks comparing signed receipts against independent records.
